questions.question: _________ is a significant festival of the Parsi people who practice Zoroastrianism as it marks the birth anniversary of Zoroaster.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Khordad Sal**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Khordad Sal** is a significant festival celebrated by the Parsi community, who practice Zoroastrianism.
 
• This festival marks the birth anniversary of **Zoroaster**, the founder of Zoroastrianism.
 
• It is a day of thanksgiving and celebration, where Parsis engage in prayers, feasting, and community activities.
 
• The festival is observed with great fervor and is considered one of the most important events in the Zoroastrian calendar.
 
• On this day, Zoroastrians reflect on the teachings of Zoroaster and reaffirm their commitment to the principles of good thoughts, good words, and good deeds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Zoroastrianism** is one of the world's oldest monotheistic religions, dating back to the 6th century BCE in ancient Persia.
 
• The religion emphasizes the duality of good and evil and the importance of individual choice in promoting good.
 
• Zoroaster, also known as Zarathustra, is considered a prophet and a spiritual leader who reformed the ancient religious practices of Persia.
 
• The Parsi community in India is one of the largest groups of Zoroastrians globally, having migrated from Persia to avoid religious persecution.
 
• Other important festivals for Zoroastrians include **Jamshed-e-Navroz** (the Persian New Year) and **Pateti** (the last day of the Zoroastrian year).

questions.question: Sheorinarayan fair is held in which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chhattisgarh.**__ 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Sheorinarayan Fair,** a renowned festival in **Chhattisgarh**, takes place annually during February's Magh Purnima.
 
• It attracts a large gathering, both local and international, to the Sheorinarayan Temple dedicated to Lord Rama, the focal point of the festivities.
 
• This event showcases the vibrant cultural heritage and traditional festivals of Chhattisgarh.
 
• Throughout the festival, the Sheorinarayan Temple is adorned with intricate decorations of lights and flowers.
 
• The temple grounds transform into bustling marketplaces, offering a diverse array of traditional crafts to visitors from across India.
 
• The atmosphere is brimming with joyous celebrations, making it a memorable occasion for all attendees.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chhattisgarh **is a landlocked state located in Central India. 
 
• It is the ninth-largest state by area and the seventeenth most populous in India, with approximately 30 million residents. 
 
• Chhattisgarh shares its borders with seven other states: Uttar Pradesh to the north, Madhya Pradesh to the northwest, Maharashtra to the southwest, Jharkhand to the northeast, Odisha to the east, and Andhra Pradesh and Telangana to the south. 
 
• Formerly a part of Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh was granted statehood on 1 November 2000, with Raipur as its designated capital.

questions.question: Which among the following festivals marks the birthday of a great Buddhist saint Je Tsongkhapa?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Galdan Namchot**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The festival that marks the birthday of the great Tibetan Buddhist saint Je **Tsongkhapa is Galdan Namchot.**
 
• This festival also marks the start of the **New Year celebrations in Ladakh, India.**
 
• **Je Tsongkhapa** was a famous** teacher of Tibetan Buddhism whose activities led to the formation of the Gelug school of Tibetan Buddhism.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sarhul: **

 
 
• Sarhul is a **tribal festival celebrated by the ethnic groups in the Indian states of Jharkhand, Odisha, and Chhattisgarh.**
 
• This festival is celebrated to mark the beginning of the new year and the arrival of spring.
 
• Sarhul is celebrated with** traditional music and dance, the worship of village deities, and the sharing of a local drink made from fermented rice or salap.**
 
 
 
• **Losar:**
 
 
• Losar is the Tibetan word for** "New Year," and it is the most important holiday in Tibet and Tibetan** **border Indian states.**
 
• It is celebrated for** 15 days, with the main celebrations on the first three days.**
 
• Losar involves ceremonies, rituals, prayers, and cultural performances, and it is a time to spend with family and friends, to exchange gifts, and to eat special foods.
 
 
 
• **Tusu:**
 
 
• Tusu is a harvest festival celebrated in the Indian states of** Jharkhand, West Bengal, and Odisha.**
 
• The festival is observed on Makar Sankranti, which usually falls on **January 14th or 15th, marking the end of the winter season and the arrival of longer days.**
 
• Tusu involves singing traditional songs, dancing, and offering prayers to **Tusu, a folk deity, for a good harvest and prosperity in the coming year.**

questions.question: In which of the following states are the Pai songs accompanied by the Saria dance sung during the rain festivals?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Madhya Pradesh** is the state where **Pai songs **are accompanied by the **Saria dance **during the **rain festivals**.
 
• The Pai songs and Saria dance are traditional cultural expressions of the local communities in Madhya Pradesh.
 
• These performances are an integral part of the rain festivals, celebrating the arrival of monsoon and the agricultural season.
 
• The festival and the associated dance and music reflect the rich cultural heritage and the agrarian lifestyle of the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Madhya Pradesh**, known as the "**Heart of India**," is renowned for its diverse culture and traditions.
 
• The state has a rich history and is home to several **UNESCO World Heritage Sites**, including the **Khajuraho Group of Monuments and the Sanchi Stupa**.
 
• The traditional music and dance forms of Madhya Pradesh, such as the Pai songs and Saria dance, play a significant role in the cultural identity of the state.
 
• The rain festivals in Madhya Pradesh not only celebrate the monsoon but also bring communities together, strengthening social bonds and fostering a sense of community.

questions.question: Rajini Gabra and Harni Gabra is the cultural festival of which of the following Indian states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Assam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rajini Gabra and Harni Gabra **are annual festivals observed by the **Dimasa tribe**.
 
• These socio-religious events are held before the commencement of new agricultural activities.
 
• The Rabha tribe celebrates the Baikho festival during the spring season to honor and seek blessings from the goddess of wealth, 'Baikho'.
 
• During this festival, the village headman, known as the 'Kunang', conducts rituals to appease the family deity by closing the village gate on the day of worship.
 
• Subsequently, on the same night, the community participates in the 'Harni Gabra' ceremony, dedicated to worshipping the presiding deity for the well-being and protection of the people.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The major festivals celebrated in Assam are Bihu, Baishagu, Ali-Ai-Ligang, Baikho, Rongker, Rajini Gabra Harni Gabra, Bohaggiyo Bishu, Ambubashi Mela and Jonbill Mela and so on.
 
• The people of Assam also celebrate Holi, Durga Puja, Diwali, Swaraswati Puja, Lakshmi Puja, Kali Puja, Idd, Muharram, Me-Dam-Me-Phi, the birth and death anniversaries of Vaishnava Saints Srimanta Sankardev and Madhabdev.
 
• The tribals of Assam have their own colourful festivals like the Kherai Puja of the Bodos, the Baikhu and Pharkantis of the Rabhas, Ali-ai-ligang and Parag of the Mishing tribe, the Sagra-misawa wansawa and laghun of the Tiwas.

questions.question: Which of the following festivals is called the month of merits and is celebrated between May and June?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Saga Dawa.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Saga Dawa:**__

 __
 
• **Saga Dawa is celebrated to mark the birth, enlightenment, and attainment of Nirvana of Gautam Buddha**.
 
• Buddha Jayanti in the **Bhutia language is called Saga Dawa.**
 
• The period for celebrating it was officially decided only in 1950, and since then, the festival has been celebrated on an annual basis.
 
• The highlight of the festival is giving alms to the needy; a virtue practiced throughout the month, conforming to the message of Buddha's life.
 
• Masks play an important role in Saga Dawa.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 **Bhanu Jayanti**
 
 
 
• It is celebrated in the state to commemorate the birth anniversary of Bhanubhakta Acharya Adikavi
 
 
 
 

 **Lossong**
 
 
 
• It is the most popular festival in Sikkim.
 
• It is usually celebrated at the end of the tenth Tibetan lunar month (usually December).
 
• It is the most important festival among the Bhutias in India and is marked by traditional Chaan dancing and merrymaking.
 
 
 
 

 **Losar**
 
 
 
• It is celebrated in the Ladakh region.
 
• The festival is celebrated on the 1st day of the eleventh month of the Tibetan Calendar.

questions.question: Which of the following is an animal trading festival of Gujarat?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vautha Mela**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vautha Mela** is an **animal** **trading **festival in the Indian state of **Gujarat**.

 
 
• It is **organized **in **November **in a village called **Vautha**.
 
• Hundreds of farmers and **traders **across India **descend **on the tiny village of **Vautha **to **trade **their **decorated donkeys **and **camels **during the Vautha Fair.
 
• The fair **lasts** for **up to five days** and includes **stalls **selling **handicrafts**, **fairground rides **and incredible local fare.
 
• Camper tents are set up near the venue, providing an unmissable opportunity to witness the trading and be a part of the festivities.
 
• This time is also **religiously significant **as the **location **happens to be the **place **where **seven holy rivers unite**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Madhavpur Mela** of **Gujarat **shares its **connection **to the **Mishmi Tribe **of **Arunachal Pradesh**.

 
 
• The festival **celebrates **the **immortal journey **which **Rukmini undertook **from **Arunachal Pradesh to Gujarat** with **Lord Krishna**.
 
• The **Mishmi** **Tribe traces **its **ancestry **to the **legendary King Bhishmak **and through him to **his daughter Rukmini** and **Lord Krishna**.
 
• This event is **commemorated **by a **cultural **fair held **every year**, **commencing **on **Ram Navami**.
 
 
 
• The **Ambubachi Mela **is an **annual Mela **held at **Kamakhya Temple in Guwahati**, Assam.
 
 
• This **four-day festival** is celebrated during the **Assamese **month of **Ahaar **(**mid-June**).
 
• The Maa **Kamakhya Devi **temple is one of **Assam’s **most** well-known temples**, and **Goddess Kamakhya is worshipped here**. 
 
• It is **believed **that this **festival **is **celebrated **to **mark **the **yearly menstruation **course of **Goddess Kamakhya**.
 
 
 
• **Kumbh Mela** is a major **pilgrimage **and **festival **in **Hinduism**.
 
 
• It is celebrated in a **cycle **of approximately **12 years**, to celebrate every **revolution Brihaspati (**Jupiter) completes, at **four river-bank pilgrimage sites**: the (**Prayagraj **(Ganges-Yamuna-Sarasvati rivers confluence), **Haridwar** (Ganges),** Nashik **(Godavari), and **Ujjain** (Shipra).
 
• The **festival **is **traditionally credited **to the 8th-century Hindu philosopher and saint **Adi Shankara**, as a part of his efforts to start major Hindu gatherings for philosophical discussions and debates along with Hindu monasteries
